claim_comment: Closing lifecycle semantics only after proving capability-gated typed unsupported behavior, feedback targeting across explicit and latent memory, bounded cancellable maintenance, verifiable forget-by-source postconditions, and compatible provider-local snapshot/replay rules.

checks.name: provider registry and handshake remain valid

acceptance_criteria: Unsupported lifecycle operations return typed unsupported results.
Feedback can target a stable item, a recall trace, or a context-pack item.
close_reason: Accepted the V1 provider lifecycle contract with explicit capability gating, latent-or-explicit feedback targets, bounded cancellable maintenance, redacted inspection, revisioned correction, verifiable source forgetting, and compatible provider-local snapshot/replay semantics.
close_comment: Evidence: provider-lifecycle-contract.json and its strict schema define a common exact-scope idempotent request context plus registry-checked health, feedback, maintenance, inspection, correction, deletion-by-source, snapshot export/restore, replay, explicit projection, and explain-trace capabilities. Unsupported optional operations return capability_unsupported with no fallback. Feedback targets exactly one stable memory ref, recall trace, or context-pack item and requires settled outcome evidence. Maintenance has finite item/byte/time limits, one writer per scope, live deadline/cancellation, partial receipts, and no unbounded scan. Inspection is bounded/redacted. Correction is revision-checked and cannot change code or Native facts. Forget-by-source reports matched/removed/anonymized/locked/remaining influence plus snapshot coverage and verification state; success cannot hide residual influence. Snapshots bind provider/build/schema/scope/generation/sequence/digest and restore cannot reset or overwrite implicitly. Replay is receipt-backed, monotonic, idempotent, and explicit about gaps/partial effects. The validator cross-checks all registry capabilities and accepted M1 contracts; mutation tests enforce unsupported, targeting, bounding, cancellation, privacy, authority, deletion postcondition, snapshot, replay, terminal, Beads, and schema rules.
